name: Constant Elevation
label: Revelation
lede: Sammy Siegler sat in on a Movielife tour around 2002 and kept Vinnie Caruana's voice in his head for sixteen years. Then he wrote his first complete songs on a tiny acoustic and asked Caruana to scream over them.

eras.title: A fill-in gig
eras.text: Siegler had drummed for Youth of Today, Judge, CIV and Rival Schools. A stint behind The Movielife showed him what Caruana could do with a hardcore song.

years.h: Siegler fills in on drums for The Movielife in Europe
years.p: The gig is short and forgettable on paper. Siegler leaves a fan of [[Vinnie Caruana|5b1ed841-450e-49b6-8bf3-b50bd54bc897]]'s voice and songwriting, and says so years later.
years.xp: No Echo traces the link to Siegler's time in Glassjaw, which put him in rooms with Long Island musicians, Caruana among them. The date is loose: Bandcamp says only "around 2002."

eras.title: Songs from a Shawn Mendes guitar
eras.text: Siegler had never written a full song start to finish. In 2018 he did, then brought the songs to Caruana, and a New York band took shape around a drummer who lives in Los Angeles.

years.big: "A miniature Taylor acoustic autographed by Shawn Mendes"
years.h: Siegler writes a whole record and calls Caruana
years.p: Siegler's description of the guitar he wrote on, left-handed and tiny. Phone demos came first; vocals were cut at Barbershop Studios, a converted church near Lake Hopatcong, New Jersey, with Brett Romnes.
years.xp:
Siegler told No Echo this was the first time he had written the music himself from start to finish. [[Alex Barreto|9e81a640-5c20-444e-9064-d2d65cf87328]] of [[Chain of Strength|81a3c11e-ac20-4bb4-8614-06b157e802d8]], [[Andrew Kline|e47911a6-1197-4b29-8ff1-5d7a3a21dc2c]] of [[Strife|5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530]] and Joe Garlipp of Despair, his bandmates in [[World Be Free|87061322-24d2-4ba9-8f25-455a44d0e354]], helped turn the phone recordings into demos.

The stone church is about 100 years old. Caruana lost his voice five minutes into tracking and finished vocals another day. His other projects lean negative, he said; these lyrics didn't.

years.cap: Sammy Siegler and Vinnie Caruana, New York, 2019
years.h: A watch store in Brooklyn hosts the first show
years.p: Constant Elevation debut at Throne on September 5, then play Trans-Pecos two days later with Luxe, Worn and Steel Cage.

years.cap: Siegler and Caruana in a record shop, 2019
years.src: Punknews · No Echo · Constant Elevation Bandcamp
years.h: Three songs, seven minutes, and a green-vinyl run in Berlin
years.p: The self-titled 7" on Revelation has Fuck Runnin', Mouth in Motion and Fletch. Punknews: "the rawest Caruana has sounded in years."
years.xp:
Punknews also called it "more hardcore than pop-punk."

CoreTex Records in Berlin sold 150 copies on opaque green vinyl alongside Revelation's pressing. Fuck Runnin' got a video; Fletch came out first as a No Echo premiere, which called it propelled by a "rhythmic thrust" and a late breakdown.

eras.title: Freedom Beach
eras.text: What began as a studio project grew into a four-piece, with players from Caspian and Pass Away.

years.h: Caspian's Jani Zubkovs joins for Freedom Beach
years.p: With guitarist Mike Ireland of Pass Away, Zubkovs plays bass on four songs cut with Jon Markson at Savaria Studios in Brooklyn, among them KRS Two and Bob X. Cursion.

sources.title: No Echo: Constant Elevation, Sammy Siegler & Vinnie Caruana join forces
